page: Hetzner Cloud cpx22 is an entry-tier virtual server from the Regular Purpose family, configured with 2 shared vCPUs based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor architecture running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16), AES, and SHA_NI. The instance allocates 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding roughly 1.95 GB of RAM per vCPU, and integrates 80 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include dedicated GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, highlighted by top-quartile results in stress-ng single-core tests and competitive single-core Geekbench scores. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into the mid-tier range, reaching 70.65 GB/sec for uncached reads and 57.5 GB/sec for uncached writes. Conversely, multi-threaded output reflects the 2-vCPU hardware ceiling and shared-core topology, producing lower-quartile performance across stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU evaluation, Clang compilation, and multi-threaded decompression tests. Network-dependent benchmarks such as static web serving throughput also register in the lower bracket at 2.41 GB/sec.

Given its shared-core execution model and compact resource envelope, Hetzner Cloud cpx22 delivers cost efficiency for workloads with low concurrency that benefit from solid single-thread performance and high-speed local NVMe storage. It is suitable for small staging environments, lightweight microservices, internal automation scripts, edge proxy routing, and low-traffic web applications.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx22 is a shared-resource virtual server featuring 2 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 4.0 GB of RAM and 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It provides broad instruction set support, including AVX-512 extensions and cryptographic acceleration flags. While synthetic benchmarks show strong single-core CPU throughput and solid large-block memory read/write speeds, overall multi-core performance is bounded by the two-thread shared-allocation model, resulting in modest PassMark and multi-threaded decompression metrics. The server lacks dedicated GPU hardware and complimentary public IPv4 addressing. With its cost-effective profile and responsive local storage, the instance is targeted at lightweight microservices, utility tasks, low-traffic web servers, and development sandboxes.
